verses.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Leave this place, you and the people you brought up out of Egypt. Go to the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I said, 'I will give it to your descendants.'
I will send an angel ahead of you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Go up to that land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go with you, because you are stubborn people, and I might destroy you on the way."
When the people heard these hard words, they were very sad, and no one put on any jewellery.

For the LORD had said to Moses, "Tell the people of Israel, 'You are stubborn people. If I went with you even for a moment, I might destroy you. Now take off your jewellery, and I will decide what to do with you.'"
So from Mount Horeb onwards, the people of Israel took off their jewellery.

Moses used to take a tent and set it up outside the camp, some distance away. He called it the Tent of Meeting. Anyone who wanted to ask the LORD something would go out to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would get up and stand at the entrances to their own tents, watching Moses until he went into the tent.
As Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stay at the entrance, while the LORD spoke with Moses.
Whenever the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, they would all stand and worship, each at the entrance of his own tent.
The LORD would speak to Moses face to face, the way a person speaks to a friend. Then Moses would go back to the camp. But his young helper Joshua son of Nun did not leave the tent.
Moses said to the LORD, "You keep telling me, 'Lead these people,' but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. You have said, 'I know you by name, and you have found favour with me.'
If I have found favour with you, please teach me your ways, so that I can know you and keep finding favour with you. And remember that this nation is your people."
The LORD answered, "I myself will go with you, and I will give you rest."
Then Moses said to him, "If you do not go with us yourself, do not send us up from here.

How else will anyone know that you are pleased with me and with your people? Only if you go with us. That is what will make me and your people different from all the other people on the face of the earth."
The LORD said to Moses, "I will do what you have asked, because you have found favour with me, and I know you by name."
Then Moses said, "Please show me your glory."

The LORD said, "I will make all my goodness pass in front of you, and I will call out my name, the LORD, in front of you. I will be kind to whom I choose to be kind, and I will show mercy to whom I choose to show mercy.
But you cannot see my face, because no one can see me and live."
Then the LORD said, "There is a place near me where you can stand on a rock.
When my glory passes by, I will put you in a crack in the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back. But my face must not be seen."
